docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: Home-improvement franchise with a visible operating benchmark
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/60667/000006066718000015/exhibit991_02022018.htm; https://corporate.lowes.com/newsroom/press-releases/lowes-announces-ceo-succession-plan-03-26-18
Date: 2018-03-26

Lowe's is a large home-improvement retailer serving household and professional repair, renovation and maintenance demand. At FY2017 end, it operated 2,152 home-improvement/hardware stores with 214.9 million square feet of selling space.

The business benefits from scale in sourcing, distribution, assortment and local store access. Bulky products, project advice and immediately available inventory make the store/distribution network economically relevant even as customers research and order digitally.

The customer base is exposed to housing and household confidence, but demand is not limited to newly built homes. Maintenance, replacement and renovation create a recurring activity base. That does not make sales recession-proof or eliminate weather and financing effects.

Home Depot provides a particularly visible competitive benchmark. Both operate large home-improvement systems, yet reported margins and sales productivity differ substantially. A peer gap is evidence worth investigating, not proof that the lower-performing company can eliminate it at no cost.

Lowe's FY2017 sales were $68.619 billion and operating income $6.586 billion, or approximately 9.6%. Home Depot's FY2017 figures were $100.904 billion and $14.681 billion, approximately 14.5%. Business mix, geography, scale and accounting all affect the comparison.

Operational improvement could involve availability, merchandising, supply chain, professional-customer service and labor productivity. These are analytical levers to investigate, not a publicly announced April 2 plan with guaranteed outcomes.

On March 26, Lowe's announced that chairman/president/CEO Robert Niblock plans to retire when a successor is appointed. The board has begun a search and Niblock remains in his roles meanwhile. No successor has been named in the qualifying information set.

January's board-refresh announcement adds a governance path: David Batchelder and Lisa Wardell joined effective March 22, with Brian Rogers to be nominated alongside them at the annual meeting. The source does not establish that a particular investor will control the board.

The core new-investment question is whether the franchise's scale and customer relevance can produce better per-share economics under a credible operating plan, and whether the valuation provides compensation for implementation and housing-cycle risk. It is not enough to label the company the cheaper member of a duopoly.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: Annual earnings, cash flow and the starting margin
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/60667/000006066718000015/exhibit991_02022018.htm; https://fiscal.ai/company/NYSE_LOW/financials/income-statement/annual/
Date: 2018-02-28

Fiscal 2017 ended February 2, 2018 and had 52 weeks; fiscal 2016 ended February 3, 2017 and had 53. Amounts are millions except EPS. The FY2015 EPS/operating-income observations are historical rows only from the modern financial database.

| Metric | FY2015 | FY2016 | FY2017 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | not independently recovered | 65,017 | 68,619 |
| Operating income | 4,971 | 5,846 | 6,586 |
| Diluted EPS | 2.73 | 3.47 | 4.09 |
| Operating margin, calculated | unavailable | 9.0% | 9.6% |
| CFO | unavailable | 5,617 | 5,065 |
| Capital expenditure | unavailable | 1,167 | 1,123 |
| CFO minus capex, calculated | unavailable | 4,450 | 3,942 |

FY2017 sales grew 5.5%, but the extra week in FY2016 distorts direct comparison. Comparable sales grew 4.0% for the year. Q4 comparable sales grew 4.1%.

The release says FY2017 program repurchases totaled approximately $3.1 billion and dividends paid approximately $1.3 billion. The retained-earnings allocation for repurchases is not total buyback cash. Buybacks reduce the share count, but sustainability depends on operating cash generation and financing capacity.

Q4 weighted-average diluted shares were 829 million and FY2017 weighted-average diluted shares 840 million. They are EPS denominators, not an exact April 2 outstanding share count.

Year-end cash was $588 million, short-term investments $102 million and long-term investments $408 million. Debt included short-term borrowings $1.137 billion, current long-term maturities $294 million and long-term debt $15.564 billion.

Total stated debt is therefore $16.995 billion; subtracting cash and both investment lines gives $15.897 billion before lease/other adjustments. Not every investment balance necessarily has the same liquidity as cash.

The 2018 outlook calls for approximately 4% sales growth and diluted EPS of $5.40-$5.50, but operating margin declining about 30bp. Tax reform and other below-operating-line effects therefore matter to the EPS growth rate.

A consolidated ROIC series and a full three-year cash-flow/lease reconciliation were not recovered. The available financial base is sufficient to frame a margin opportunity, but not to assert that peer-level margins or historical capital returns are inevitable.
docs.D03_latest_results.md:
Title: Fourth-quarter miss and a forward margin challenge
Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/60667/000006066718000015/exhibit991_02022018.htm
Date: 2018-02-28

Lowe's reported Q4 sales of $15.494 billion and net earnings of $554 million. Diluted EPS was $0.67, compared with $0.74 a year earlier; the prior-year quarter had an additional week.

Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.74 versus $0.86. Adjustments matter, but even the adjusted comparison shows weaker quarterly per-share results despite positive comparable sales.

Q4 comparable sales increased 4.1%. The quarter therefore does not present a simple collapse in customer demand. The challenge is converting sales and scale into earnings while managing costs and investments.

FY2017 net earnings were approximately $3.4 billion and diluted EPS $4.09. Sales were $68.619 billion. The annual record shows a meaningful earnings franchise, not a company whose operating model has ceased to generate cash.

The company ended the year with 2,152 stores and 214.9 million selling square feet. This physical base can support assortment, local availability and project demand, but it also creates execution complexity and fixed operating costs.

For FY2018, management expects sales to increase approximately 4% and operating margin to decline approximately 30 basis points. It forecasts diluted EPS of $5.40-$5.50. The expected EPS increase cannot be interpreted as equivalent operating-margin improvement.

The fiscal-year comparison includes tax and special-item effects. A successful operating-repair model should explicitly separate total revenue growth, operating margin, tax rate and share count rather than use guided EPS as proof that all levers are already fixed.

Cash generation remains substantial: FY2017 CFO was $5.065 billion and capex $1.123 billion. The simple difference is $3.942 billion, before dividends, debt changes and other investing/financing movements.

The quarter creates an actionable analytical question: are weak earnings conversion and lower margin guidance symptoms of fixable merchandising, supply-chain or productivity issues, or do they reflect structural competitive disadvantages?

No post-cutoff earnings, new CEO appointment or subsequent turnaround targets are used to answer that question. The March 26 CEO-search announcement changes the governance context, but the eventual replacement and operating plan remain unknown at the assigned cutoff.
docs.D04_price_valuation.md:
Title: April price and the earnings/margin bridge
Source: compiled from: https://fiscal.ai/company/NYSE_LOW/; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/60667/000006066718000015/exhibit991_02022018.htm; https://ir.homedepot.com/~/media/Files/H/HomeDepot-IR/reports-and-presentations/quarterly-earnings/q4-2017-press-release.pdf
Date: 2018-04-02

Historical daily data show Lowe's opening at $87.35 and closing at $84.59 on April 2, on volume of 9,611,700 shares. Only that historical row is used; the database's current operating description and later forecasts are excluded.

The close implies 20.7x FY2017 GAAP EPS of $4.09. Against FY2018 guided EPS midpoint of $5.45, it implies 15.5x. These multiples use known company results/guidance rather than an invented consensus estimate.

The large difference between trailing and forward multiples needs explanation. Management simultaneously forecasts an operating-margin decline, so the EPS increase incorporates tax, share-count and other effects; it is not solely an operating turnaround.

Q4 diluted weighted shares of 829 million give an indicative equity-size proxy of $70.125 billion at the close. This is not exact market capitalization because weighted-average diluted shares are not April spot outstanding shares.

Year-end debt totaled $16.995 billion and cash/investments $1.098 billion. Adding that simple net-debt measure to the equity proxy gives approximately $86.022 billion before leases and other adjustments.

The same equity proxy against FY2017 CFO-minus-capex of $3.942 billion gives roughly 5.6%. This is a backward-looking cash-flow yield proxy, not a normalized forecast or an exact current-market calculation.

The margin sensitivity is material. Each 100bp of operating margin on FY2017 revenue equals approximately $686 million of annual EBIT, before taxes, required investment and changes in revenue. This is an explicit arithmetic sensitivity, not a forecast that the improvement occurs.

Home Depot's FY2017 margin of about 14.5% exceeds Lowe's 9.6% by approximately 490bp. Eliminating that entire gap would be an aggressive scenario requiring justification about mix, productivity, investment and execution; the gap alone is not intrinsic value.

A verified April 52-week range, daily historical-multiple series, contemporaneous S&P multiple and forward peer P/Es were not recovered. The supported valuation analysis is the observed price versus guidance and a clearly labeled margin sensitivity, with implementation and cycle risk left visible.
docs.D05_market_concerns.md:
Title: Why the operating discount may persist
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/60667/000006066718000015/exhibit991_02022018.htm; https://www.bizjournals.com/charlotte/news/2018/03/26/niblock-to-retire-as-activist-members-join-lowe-s.html; https://corporate.lowes.com/newsroom/press-releases/lowes-announces-ceo-succession-plan-03-26-18
Date: 2018-03-26

The company's February results show the tension clearly: comparable sales grew, yet adjusted quarterly EPS fell and the 2018 outlook included a lower operating margin. A valuation discount may reflect concern about execution rather than merely irrational pessimism.

The March 26 Charlotte Business Journal report places Niblock's planned retirement after activist-linked board changes. It points out that no successor is waiting to take over. That is a concrete contemporaneous uncertainty, not a known resolution.

A CEO search creates optionality but can also delay decisions, distract operating teams and produce a candidate without the required retail-transformation skills. A better operating plan cannot be assumed solely because the incumbent will leave.

The peer gap can also contain structural components. Differences in professional-customer mix, assortment, local market density and distribution productivity may not be eliminated quickly. Higher investment may be necessary before margin improves.

Housing exposure adds a separate risk. Repair/maintenance demand is more recurring than new construction, but household confidence, rates, turnover and discretionary projects can affect spending. A turnaround begun during a favorable cycle may look easier than it proves in weaker conditions.

Debt matters. The year-end balance sheet includes approximately $17 billion stated debt before lease adjustments. Strong cash generation provides support, but operational underperformance and continued capital return can compete for that cash.

The favorable case is that the customer franchise and scale remain valuable while execution falls below potential. Under that interpretation, specific fixes in inventory, merchandising, pro service, distribution and labor productivity can improve returns without requiring a new market.

That favorable view needs milestones: service/availability, sales productivity, sustainable margin improvement and disciplined reinvestment. An investor should not rely on an eventual celebrity hire, a guaranteed peer multiple or a fixed timetable absent from the public record.

The pack excludes the May appointment of the next CEO, any later operating targets and the manager's eventual stake announcement. It therefore preserves the real April uncertainty: attractive underlying assets and a visible performance gap, but only an open search rather than a completed management upgrade.
docs.D06_peer_industry.md:
Title: The Home Depot benchmark — what the gap does and does not prove
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/60667/000006066718000015/exhibit991_02022018.htm; https://ir.homedepot.com/~/media/Files/H/HomeDepot-IR/reports-and-presentations/quarterly-earnings/q4-2017-press-release.pdf
Date: 2018-02-28

Home Depot is the most directly relevant scale benchmark. The companies share broad home-improvement demand, store/distribution infrastructure and both household and professional customers. The comparison is still imperfect because their customer, geographic and operational mixes differ.

| FY2017 measure | Lowe's | Home Depot |
|---|---:|---:|
| Revenue | $68.619bn | $100.904bn |
| Operating income | $6.586bn | $14.681bn |
| Calculated operating margin | 9.6% | 14.5% |
| Diluted EPS | $4.09 | $7.29 |
| Comparable sales growth | 4.0% | 6.8% |
| CFO | $5.065bn | $12.031bn |
| Capex | $1.123bn | $1.897bn |

Home Depot reported sales per square foot of $417.02. Lowe's year-end selling-area figure is not a matched weighted-average denominator, so a directly comparable productivity ratio is not manufactured by dividing annual sales by year-end area.

The approximately 490bp reported operating-margin gap indicates meaningful potential economic value if even part is fixable. Each 100bp on Lowe's sales base is about $686 million EBIT before taxes, reinvestment and any growth.

However, peer-level margin is not an automatic entitlement. Home Depot's larger scale, mix and operating systems may support durable advantages. Some catch-up spending can depress near-term earnings before benefits appear.

The balance-sheet/cash-flow comparison is also important: Home Depot's FY2017 CFO-minus-capex was approximately $10.134 billion, versus Lowe's $3.942 billion. Different scale accounts for part, but the data show why current profit conversion deserves attention.

Home Depot's 2018 outlook includes approximately 14.5% operating margin, while Lowe's projects a 30bp decline from its lower base. The public forward evidence does not yet show the gap narrowing.

Complete timestamped valuation and margin tables for additional peers were not recovered. Smaller specialty retailers or general merchandisers would be less direct benchmarks, and no two-to-four-peer valuation ranking is invented.

The investable thesis must identify which parts of the gap are operationally addressable, by whom and at what cost. A lower P/E without a credible bridge from current execution to improved cash earnings is not enough.
docs.D07_event_context.md:
Title: Board changes and an unresolved CEO search
Source: compiled from: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/lowes-announces-three-new-appointments-to-board-of-directors-300585116.html; https://corporate.lowes.com/newsroom/press-releases/lowes-announces-ceo-succession-plan-03-26-18; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/60667/000006066718000015/exhibit991_02022018.htm
Date: 2018-04-02

**January 19:** Lowe's announces appointments of David Batchelder, co-founder of Relational Investors, and Lisa Wardell, CEO of Adtalem, effective March 22. Brian Rogers, chairman/former CIO of T. Rowe Price, is to be nominated with them for election at the annual meeting.

The board additions create a potential oversight and capital-allocation catalyst. They do not establish that all directors agree on a turnaround plan, that an activist controls the company or that a particular CEO will be selected.

**February 28:** FY2017 results show a large, profitable retailer with a substantial margin gap to Home Depot. The 2018 outlook forecasts EPS growth but operating-margin decline. That makes operating execution a live issue rather than a completed repair.

**March 22:** The announced effective date for Batchelder and Wardell joining the board arrives. There is no need to backdate later annual-meeting outcomes into this snapshot.

**March 26:** Niblock announces his plan to retire after a 25-year company career when a successor is appointed. He remains chairman, president and CEO during the search. The company says the board has initiated that search.

**April 2:** The share price closes at $84.59. A new investor sees a scaled franchise, a visible peer gap, refreshed oversight and an open succession process. The eventual hire, appointment date and plan are not known.

Precise current Pershing AUM, cash and name-by-name weights were not recovered from an authenticated pre-cutoff update. The manager's historical concentrated ownership approach is relevant, but it is not a quantitative capacity estimate or evidence that a Lowe's stake has already been announced.

The earnings release also identifies conversion, gross margin and inventory management as execution priorities. Those are already public management objectives, not a later investor-authored plan. No later manager purchase disclosure is included.

The decision can therefore be conditional: whether the starting valuation and likely operating opportunity warrant capital before a CEO is named, or whether management/plan evidence is still insufficient. The model should not treat a future high-caliber appointment as an April fact or claim that the manager personally installed the eventual CEO.

drivers.driver: Scaled home-improvement franchise with durable repair/renovation demand.
Close operating-margin and productivity gap to Home Depot through merchandising, inventory/supply chain, pro-customer service and expense execution.
Confidence in Marvin Ellison's relevant Home Depot experience and management upgrade; this was not yet public at April2 cutoff.
Cash generation and buybacks improve per-share value alongside operating repair.

answer_key.pack_quality_notes: Seven documents; public succession search, not eventual Ellison appointment. April cutoff precedes critical later management evidence and is a timing-mismatch stress case, not perfectly observed first execution. Authentic Lowe/HomeDepot tables, price/volume. Current AUM, exact entry day, full2015financials and wider peer valuations missing.

valuation.eps_path: 4% revenue growth combined with 100-200bp margin expansion as the efficiency gap closes
valuation.downside_case: Limited by duopoly market position and strong FCF generation

drivers.driver: The company is a dominant, cash-generative player in a stable home-improvement duopoly with high barriers to entry.
We are able to acquire our stake at 15.5x forward earnings, which is a significant discount to historical levels and peer multiples for a business of this quality.
The current 490bp operating margin gap compared to Home Depot is a fixable performance deficit rather than a structural failure.
The CEO succession process and recent board refreshment provide a catalyst to drive operational improvement and capital allocation efficiency.

kill_criteria: New CEO fails to prioritize or execute on closing the operating margin gap against the primary competitor.
Comparable sales growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters.
The company resorts to significant debt-funded acquisitions or capital-allocation policies that degrade the balance sheet.
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the 490bp operating margin gap is structural and immutable, or a fundamental deterioration in the duopoly competitive dynamic.
final.memo:
Lowe's is a dominant, free-cash-flow-generative home-improvement retailer that operates in a stable duopoly with high barriers to entry [D01]. Despite generating $3.942 billion in free cash flow in 2017, the company has significantly underperformed its primary competitor in operational efficiency [D01, D02].

The market currently views Lowe's 490bp operating margin disadvantage as a permanent competitive failure and is further deterred by the uncertainty surrounding the CEO transition [D01, D05, D07]. We believe this perspective is incorrect, as the margin gap represents a fixable performance deficit that can be addressed through better operational execution [D01, D06].

We have the opportunity to acquire shares at approximately 15.5x forward earnings [D04]. With consistent 4% comparable sales growth and the potential for 100-200bp of margin expansion, we expect to achieve an attractive double-digit internal rate of return as the market re-rates the business toward a 20x multiple upon successful turnaround [D01, D02, D06].

Our role as a shareholder will be to engage privately with the newly refreshed board to ensure the appointment of a leader capable of executing on operational improvements [D01, D07]. We intend to advocate for a clear strategy focused on closing the margin gap and optimizing capital allocation [D01, D06].

We recognize the primary risk is that the margin gap may prove structural; however, the business's strong cash flow and duopoly position provide a significant cushion against downside [D01, D02]. We are initiating a position today with a target of 8% of our portfolio, as we believe this is a high-quality compounder temporarily mispriced due to fixable execution headwinds [D01, D05].

valuation.eps_path: Mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth plus 300-400 bps margin expansion, targeting $8.00-$8.50 in 3-5 years
valuation.downside_case: Multiple contraction to 12-14x if margin gap persists, but limited permanent capital loss due to scale moats

drivers.driver: Lowe's is a dominant, free-cash-flow-generative home improvement retailer with significant scale and durable competitive advantages.
A 490 basis point operating margin gap compared to Home Depot represents a major, remediable operational underperformance rather than a structural disadvantage.
Recent board refreshes and the announced CEO transition provide a powerful catalyst to drive operational change and margin parity.
The stock trades at an attractive 15.5x 2018 guidance, offering significant upside as earnings power is unlocked.

kill_criteria: New management fails to articulate or execute a credible plan to close the operating margin gap within 24 months.
Comparable sales growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters.
The company initiates significant debt-funded acquisitions that deviate from the core home-improvement focus.
The housing market experiences a structural downturn that impairs long-term FCF generation capacity.
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the margin gap is structurally locked due to unavoidable operational inefficiencies that new leadership cannot fix.
final.memo:
Lowe's Companies is a dominant player in the home improvement industry, operating over 2,100 stores that provide stable, recurring demand for repair and renovation [D01]. The business is inherently simple and cash-generative, underpinned by massive scale in sourcing and distribution that creates significant barriers to entry [D01, D02].

We believe the market significantly misjudges Lowe's, viewing its 9.6% operating margin as structurally inferior to Home Depot’s 14.5% [D01, D06]. Our analysis suggests this 490 basis point gap is not a permanent feature of the business, but a symptom of remediable operational underperformance [D01].

With the recent retirement announcement of the CEO and the appointment of new board members in March 2018, the necessary catalysts for change are now in place [D01, D07]. We expect new leadership to prioritize supply chain rationalization and inventory management to bridge this performance gap over the next three to five years [D01].

We have acquired our position at 15.5x FY2018 earnings guidance, a valuation that does not fully reflect the potential for normalized margins and mid-to-high single-digit earnings growth [D01, D04]. We anticipate this will drive substantial value creation, with expected returns in the low-twenties percent range [D03].

The primary risk remains that the margin differential proves more structural than expected, limiting our ability to drive convergence [D01, D05]. However, given the strength of the company's core franchise and its resilient balance sheet, we view the downside as protected [D01, D02].

We are initiating a 10% position in Lowe's, consistent with our strategy of investing in high-quality businesses undergoing positive management transitions [D01, Rule 5]. We will work quietly with the board and new management to support the execution of these improvements.
